newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines flat as supply builds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines flat as supply builds.

text.p: Traders said U.S. West Coast gasoline prices did not change Wednesday, as fears of supply tightness faded following the return of a major refinery and inventory builds.
Exxon's 135,000 barrel-per-day refinery east of San Francisco ran at full capacity after several units, including the coker and hydrocracker, were shut two months ago for planned maintenance.
Traders said the refinery's lost output helped put pressure on wholesale prices last week, lifting CARB gasoline about 6.5 cents last week.
Traders said said major refineries avoided buying, but at least one tried selling crude in San Francisco.
Traders dismissed rumors parts of Unocal's California refineries shut yesterday because of worker layoffs.
Union negotiators agreed earlier this week to a new contract with Tosco, which will buy the plants from Unocal next week and plans to reduce staff by 15 percent.
Local officials said concerns about the number of layoffs could jeopardize the contract.

Meanwhile, the supplies out west rose last week, with American Petroleum Institute (AP) reporting Tuesday that stocks of West Coast gasoline climbed 861,000 barrels from an 11-year low of 25.6 million the week before.
Wholesale prices for conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles remained 82/83 cents a gallon, while CARB gasoline held at Tuesday's 86/87-cent range.
Sellers came forward in the San Francisco gasoline market, hoping to take advantage of a two-cent profit as Bay grades rose to parity with L.A. amid Exxon's maintenance, traders said.
"Give the Bay and take L.A.," one broker said.
